author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

body:
Fixes #9223 
<!-- 
Describe the changes you have made here: what, why, ... 
Link issues that are fixed, e.g. "Fixes #333".
If you fixed a koppor issue, link it, e.g. "Fixes https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/47".
The title of the PR must not reference an issue, because GitHub does not support autolinking there.
-->


## Issue description
The content of the dialog for the cleanup entries becomes partially visible when resizing the 
dialog (decreasing the size) vertically or horizontally.

## Solution description
I added a *ScrollPane* and put the content of the *presetPanel* inside this ScrollPane in order to
be able to scroll and view the rest of the content when needed (when the dialog is resized).

**Note:** I put the name of the ScrollPane Object as `scrollPane` but I believe the name can be more significant and coherent 
with the project structure.

I also changed the preferred height to 650, so when the dialog opens, it displays all the initial information without the need 
to display the scroll bar.

### The new CleanupDialog

![Screenshot from 2022-10-11 23-43-07](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/82417779/195213288-241e62f3-2173-422c-bb7c-e94d58f9feb5.png)

## Other possible enhancements
While fixing this issue, i noticed that the *CleanupDialog* can be resized with no limits. In other words the size of the dialog 
can be reduced to 0 or extended to infinity, as show the pictures below: 

![Screenshot from 2022-10-12 00-00-43](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/82417779/195213816-bee2e86d-d263-4b84-bcf0-156101f4f086.png)

![Screenshot from 2022-10-12 00-07-17](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/82417779/195214432-1719620f-5d3f-42b4-981e-4cc5a7dc41ee.png)

So we can add *min-width* and *min-height* for the Dialog.

body:
Adds fuzz tests for the grant parser. Running this I found two issues:

* We were not consistently handling invalid unicode. I fixed this by always replacing invalid unicode in inputs with the unicode replacement handler. This is what marshaling to JSON already does.
* We were not handling empty output fields consistently. `output_fields=,` was allowed while `output_fields=` was not. Now the latter is allowed and the former is equal to the latter.

body: # [Portfolio: accessibility](https://github.com/microverseinc/curriculum-html-css/blob/main/portfolio/6_accessability.md) ## Review of Web Accessibility In the phase of the portfolio project, the following checks were carried out and accessibility issue #12 fix where applicable: ### [Page titles](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary/#title) In the head section of the [index.html](https://github.com/fmanimashaun/My-Portfolio/blob/main/index.html) file, the `title` tag was used to indicate the page title `HOME | PERSONAL PORTFOLIO`. This was chosen to turn the entire portfolio site into a multi-page site in the future. ### [Image text alternatives** (``)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary/#images) In the body section of the [index.html](https://github.com/fmanimashaun/My-Portfolio/blob/main/index.html) file, we have 22 `img` tags with their respective `alt` text. The web developer extension chrome was used to confirm further the correct use of the `alt` text. ### [Text headings](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary/#headings) A check was run on each page section to ensure the correct use of heading tags within all sections. A few adjusted were made to the hero section to ensure the heading tags were properly placed, and the about and contact section tags were replaced with `div` based on the [W3 HTML validator](https://validator.w3.org/nu/doc=https%3A%2F%2Ffmanimashaun.github.io%2FMy-Portfolio%2F#textarea) recommendation after the checks. ### [Color contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary/#contrast) The about me section list item's text color was changed `#008552` to improve the contrast ratio. ### [Resize](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary/#resize) The browser zoom setting was varied to see the wrap effect on the entire layout as the zoom percentage increases. The page responded positively by wrapping text where appropriate and increasing the text size in response to the zoom setting. ### [Interaction](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary/#interaction) For screen reader accessibility, the placeholder text was included to account for the absence of a label. And texted with a screen reader to ensure the audio feedback matches the text and the functionality requirements of the form inputs. Also, visual feedback was added to the buttons for keyboard use concerning user accessibility. ### [Moving content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary/#moving) NA ### [Multimedia](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary/#media) NA ### [The basic structure of the page](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary/#structure) The page's overall structure looks good when the styles are disabled, all images display their `alt` text when the image is disabled, and every block of text has a clear heading.
